newsitem.title: UK: East Europe rally to continue, insulated from Fed.
newsitem.headline: East Europe rally to continue, insulated from Fed.

text.p: East European equity markets will continue their gains in to 1997 and the region is effectively insulated from U.S. monetary tightening, ING Barings said in a research report.
"The fundamental story remains positive and, for the most part, market momentum is likely to spill over in to 1997," said Philip Poole, director of emerging Europe research.
ING Barings favoured equity markets in the region are Russia and Poland, and among fixed income assets, Russia, Hungary and the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

It notes that not only do the region's markets have an extremely low correlation with developed markets, but they also offer a good diversification tool for dedicated emerging markets investors in Asia and Latin America.
"Price return data highlight a stronger relationship between emerging European fixed income markets and German rates than is the case for links with the U.S. market," Poole said.
